omeprazole: Proton pump inhibitor: blocks the acid pump (H+/K+ ATPase), the final step whatever the stimulus; more acid suppression than an H2 blocker
Give 30 to 60 minutes before breakfast (ACG 2022; label: before meals)
C. diff diarrhea any time, especially in hospital; low magnesium after 3+ months (label)
famotidine: H2 (histamine 2) receptor blocker: blocks 1 of 3 signals, so less acid, not none
Works within about an hour; with or without food
CrCl under 60: lower dose; confusion or delirium reported in older adults and with moderate or severe kidney impairment (label)

memory_line: Omeprazole: pump off. Famotidine: signal off.
caption_lesson:
🧪 First, how the stomach makes acid
• Cells in the stomach lining push acid out through tiny pumps (proton pumps)
• A meal switches the pumps on. Histamine is 1 of 3 signals that do it (with gastrin and a nerve signal)

🩵 Omeprazole (PUMP OFF)
• A PPI (proton pump inhibitor): blocks the pump itself, the last step, whatever the signal. More acid cut than famotidine
• Give it 30 to 60 minutes before breakfast: it blocks pumps that a meal switches on. The full effect builds over a few days
• Swallow the capsule whole. Don't crush or chew it
• Any time, especially in the hospital: C. diff (Clostridioides difficile) diarrhea. Report diarrhea that won't go away
• On it 3 months or more: low magnesium. Check the level as ordered

💜 Famotidine (SIGNAL OFF)
• An H2 (histamine 2) blocker: blocks the histamine signal, so less acid, not none
• Works within about an hour, with or without food
• Cleared by the kidneys: CrCl (creatinine clearance) under 60 means a lower dose
• Confusion or delirium can happen in older adults and with weak kidneys: report it

✅ The right move
• Omeprazole: 30 to 60 minutes before breakfast
• Famotidine: check kidney function, watch for confusion

rn_checks: Omeprazole: PPI, blocks the H+/K+ ATPase, the final step whatever the stimulus (label 12.1); more acid suppression than an H2 blocker (ACG 2022). On screen 'more acid cut', not 'the most'. OK?
Timing: 30 to 60 minutes before breakfast for once-daily dosing (ACG 2022); the label says before meals. OK?

Warnings: C. diff diarrhea with PPI therapy, especially in hospitalized patients (any time); low magnesium after 3+ months, most after a year (label 5.3, 5.9). Swallow the capsule whole (label 2.3). Bone fracture and B12 left out for the 3-fact limit. OK?

Famotidine: H2 blocker, onset within 1 hour, with or without food; CrCl under 60 mL/min: lower dose; CNS reactions (confusion, delirium) reported in older adults and in moderate or severe kidney impairment; QT prolongation reported with kidney impairment (label 2, 5.1, 8.6). QT is in the RN check only, not the caption. OK?
On screen: '1 of 3 signals off: less acid, not none' (histamine; gastrin and acetylcholine still act). OK?
Memory words are NEW: omeprazole (PUMP OFF), famotidine (SIGNAL OFF). Keep or swap?
Drawing choices: one stomach lining (parietal) cell, three acid pumps on the stomach side, the histamine receptor on the blood side; acid as H+ dots; magnesium dots; pump counts are illustrative
Pick answer B (30 to 60 min before breakfast, about 7:00); keyword PHARM; hook, cover and caption line 1 open with 'Nurses:'
30-day rule: no omeprazole, famotidine or acid-reducer Reel in the last 30 days. OK?
